The new tests pass because `_settings()` omits `GITEA.URL` unless a test supplies it, which no real run does.

The effect is that this issue's own scenario regresses: an operator whose `GITEA__URL` is the internal API address gets that address back in links unless they also set `GITEA__WEB_URL`, which is what the derivation was there to avoid. Preferring the configured value only when it differs from the shipped default would keep both behaviours.

Can you fix this one? I hope it helps.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
Good catch — fixed in 2fb22278. You're right on both counts: `configuration.toml` always ships `url = "https://gitea.com"`, so the truthiness check made the derivation unreachable, and the `_settings()` helper omitting `GITEA.URL` is exactly why the suite stayed green against a condition no real run has.

Done as you suggested: the configured value now only wins when it differs from the shipped default. The resolver rstrips and compares `GITEA.URL` against a new `DEFAULT_GITEA_URL` module constant, which `__init__` also uses as its fallback so the two can't drift. Precedence: `GITEA.WEB_URL` → non-default `GITEA.URL` → derived from `pr.html_url` → `base_url`. The operator with an internal `GITEA__URL` and no `GITEA__WEB_URL` gets the `html_url` derivation again; an explicitly configured URL still beats a stale server `ROOT_URL`.

Two regression tests added, this time supplying `GITEA.URL` the way a real run does: the exact shipped default, and a trailing-slash variant — neither shadows the derivation anymore. The `configuration.toml` comment and `gitea.md` now state the new precedence. `tests/unittest/test_gitea_provider.py`: 36 passed.
